title: Research
text:
PhD
My PhD (completed 2022) used a substantial body of existing seabird tracking data to determine the role of habitat accessibility and preference in explaining variation in distribution patterns, both within and between seabird species.

title: Research
text:
Research assistant
I conducted quality assurance and control on several seabird population distribution databases (spanning 500 individual populations and 60 years) in preparation for further analysis.

title: Research
text:
Honours
I investigated the physiological and environmental factors influencing the field body temperature and movement patterns of estuarine crocodiles in the Wenlock River system, Northern Queensland. This project involved refining and analysing over 9 million raw data points in R (including GAM, GLMM, and FFT analyses, and data visualisation using ggplot2).

title: Research
text:
Undergraduate project
I studied the frequency of skin sloughing in two native Australian amphibians, and its relationship with body size.

title: Research
text:
Volunteering
I’ve also assisted with data collection for projects on kangaroo social behaviour and endocrinology, as well as native fish passage through culverts.
For publications, see my Google Scholar profile.

Small-group tutorials for third-year students on animal social and eusocial behaviour, personality, signalling and communication, and family interactions, plus essay writing, communication and presentation skills.

I am a researcher interested in the causes and consequences of animal movement, and the emerging technologies that we can use to track animals in the wild. I am especially concerned with changes in animal movement behaviour caused by climate change.
I’m currently a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science, based at the University of Queensland. I work with Associate Professor Daniel Dunn in the Applied Marine Biogeography Lab on projects related to migratory connectivity in the ocean.
In 2022 I completed my PhD as a Gates Cambridge scholar, in partnership with the Department of Zoology and the British Antarctic Survey, on albatross and petrel foraging ecology.
I spent most of 2017 undertaking a Data Science fellowship in the Kampala office of Fenix International, a solar power company bringing affordable clean energy to off-grid customers in Uganda.
My previous research was in the Franklin ECO-Lab at the University of Queensland, where I investigated saltwater crocodile thermal biology and movement ecology.
Outside of academia, I worked for eight years in Animal Training & Behaviour at the RSPCA Queensland, teaching obedience, agility, puppy classes, and individual training.
Find out more about my Research, Teaching and Outreach, or see my publications on Google Scholar.
